_comment: Classification of every declared input GOPAL's shipped policies read, against what a standard Hugging Face model card structurally contains. A judgement, written out field by field so it can be argued with. 'Answerable' means the card itself establishes the fact, without inference or inspecting the repository around it. Anything absent from both lists is untouched by a card.
_card_structure: YAML: license, language, datasets, metrics, model-index, base_model, pipeline_tag, library_name, tags

Sections: Model Details, Uses (Direct / Downstream / Out-of-Scope), Bias Risks and Limitations, How to Get Started, Training Details, Evaluation, Environmental Impact, Technical Specifications, Citation

answerable.accuracy.metrics_declared: `model-index` / the Evaluation section is exactly a declaration of metrics
answerable.governance.third_party_model_in_use: `base_model` in the YAML names the upstream model

partial.model.general_purpose: `pipeline_tag` and `library_name` hint at it, but GPAI is a legal classification with a compute threshold
partial.model.cumulative_training_compute_flops: Training Details and Environmental Impact sometimes give compute, rarely FLOPs
partial.datasets.relevant: the `datasets` field names them; relevance is a claim about them
partial.datasets.sufficiently_representative: Bias, Risks and Limitations often discusses representativeness without asserting it
partial.datasets.errors_addressed: not asserted by any card section
partial.datasets.complete_to_the_extent_possible: not asserted by any card section
partial.datasets.contextual_characteristics_cons: Article 10(4) asks about the deployment setting, which a card rarely knows
partial.accuracy.declared_in_instructions: the card is documentation; whether it is the instructions for use is a legal question
partial.documentation.technical_documentation.co: a card is a summary, not the Annex IV file
partial.documentation.testing_process_documented: Evaluation covers results more often than process
partial.transparency.ai_use_disclosed: disclosure is to the affected person, not in the card
partial.robustness.performance_thresholds_define: metrics are given; thresholds are a decision about them
partial.training_content.public_summary_availabl: the Training Data section is arguably one, which is untested
partial.training_content.summary_sufficiently_de: sufficiency is judged against Article 53(1)(d), not the card
partial.fairness.bias_assessment_completed: Bias, Risks and Limitations is a discussion, not a completed assessment
partial.fairness.protected_characteristics_teste: named occasionally, and rarely as a tested set
partial.fairness.max_disparity: only if fairness metrics happen to be reported
partial.system.sources: the `datasets` field can indicate provenance of training images
partial.model.free_and_open_source: `license` names a licence, but the Article 53(2) open-source treatment also turns on access, use, modification and distribution rights and on parameters being public. A licence string is evidence toward the test, not the test
partial.model.parameters_publicly_available: established by inspecting the repository, not by the card. A card may link weights without asserting their availability
partial.documentation.model_card.completeness: circular: the card scoring itself. Counting it as answerable inflates the numerator
